newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Sweden's Malmo Aviation buys 40 pct of Cityjet.
newsitem.headline: Sweden's Malmo Aviation buys 40 pct of Cityjet.

text.p: Swedish airline Malmo Aviation said on Wednesday it would become a part owner of Irish airline Cityjet with a 40 percent stake and an option to increase this.

"Malmo Aviation has reached an agreement with a group of Irish investors to become a 40 percent and largest owner in Irish airline Cityjet with a long-term possibility to become a majority owner," Malmo Aviation said in a statment.
It said Cityjet's most important routes were between London City Airport and Dublin and London City Airport and Paris.
"Cityjet, which has been in operation for three years, is now going through a financial reconstruction," said the Swedish airline, based in the southern Swedish city of Malmo.

At the same time Malmo Aviation said it had signed a code-sharing agreement with Air UK on routes between Sweden and Britain. Air UK is Britain's third largest airline and Royal Dutch Airline KLM is the largest owner.
"Both of these deals that we have been offered indicate our investment in London has been right," Malmo Aviation managing director Hans Kallenius said in the statement.
Malmo Aviation flies to Stockholm's Bromma Airport, west coast city Gothenburg and London City Airport.
